title: Effect of High-Dose Vitamin D Supplementation on Volumetric Bone Density and Bone Strength: A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Burt LA, Billington EO, Rose MS, Raymond DA, Hanley DA, Boyd SK
population: Community-dwelling adults aged 55 to 70 years in Calgary, Canada, with serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D 30 to 125 nmol/L and without osteoporosis; calcium supplements given to those with dietary intake below 1200 mg/day
funder: Funding was provided by Pure North S'Energy Foundation in response to an investigator-initiated research grant proposal. Pure North S'Energy Foundation had no role in the design and conduct of the study, data collection, analysis, manuscript preparation or the decision to publish. Registry: lead sponsor University of Calgary; collaborator Pure North S'Energy Foundation.
inKindSupport: Vitamin D3 drops (80, 800 or 2000 IU per drop) were provided and checked for quality by Ddrops Canada; finite element software was provided free of charge by Numerics88 Solutions, co-owned by an author.
authorConflicts: Billington: grants and scientific advisory board fees from Amgen and Eli Lilly. Hanley: grants and speaker honoraria from Amgen and grants from Eli Lilly. Boyd: co-owner of Numerics88 Solutions; panel honorarium from Amgen.
result: Vitamin D3 400 IU (n=109), 4000 IU (n=100) or 10,000 IU (n=102) daily for 3 years; 287 (92%) completed. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D at baseline, 3 months and 3 years: 76.3, 76.7 and 77.4 nmol/L (400 IU); 81.3, 115.3 and 132.2 (4000 IU); 78.4, 188.0 and 144.4 (10,000 IU). Radial total volumetric BMD fell by 1.2%, 2.4% and 3.5%, and tibial by 0.4%, 1.0% and 1.7%, respectively; against 400 IU, radial differences were -3.9 mg HA/cm3 (95% CI -6.5 to -1.3) at 4000 IU and -7.5 (-10.1 to -5.0) at 10,000 IU, tibial -1.8 (-3.7 to 0.1) and -4.1 (-6.0 to -2.2). Failure load did not differ between groups. Participants with at least one episode of hypercalcaemia: 0 (400 IU), 4 (4%; 4000 IU), 9 (9%; 10,000 IU); hypercalciuria 19 (17%), 22 (22%), 34 (33%). Falls 4 (4%), 10 (10%), 5 (5%); low-trauma fractures 4, 3 and 5. Serious adverse events 16 (15%), 8 (8%), 14 (14%); one death (presumed myocardial infarction) in the 400 IU group. An erratum was published (JAMA 2019;322:1925).
